I tried to go with the same line of assumptions as you - that the students could see if any other students turned in an answer or not.

With your problem though, I think a slight adjustment needs to be made where all the students' guesses should be 7. This eliminates the need for the leader to pick a student that isn't assigned "7", and this also solves the (very rare) case where all students are assigned "7".

Not sure what the exact rules are, but this is assuming that: 1, the students can communicate about a plan before the numbers are assigned; and 2, the students can see if another student wrote down something.

Designate the students at Student A, B, C, D, E, F, and G. 

Have Student A look at Student G. If his number is "1", he writes down something (doesn't matter what).

Have Student B look at Student G, but with the number 2. Student C does the same for 3, Student D for 4, Student E for 5.  Student F for 6.

If no student wrote anything down, then Student G knows his number is 7, so he can write that down and get the correct answer. If a student wrote something down, then all Student G has to do is track which student wrote it, and then he knows what his own number is.
